draft_notes.explanation: Enumerate exact clipped corner-bracket frames for every foreground colour. Every noncentral frame must have at least2 visible corner brackets; centres may be anywhere including outside the grid. Enumerate both complete radius assignments0..m-1 and1..m simultaneously, allowing either a visible or background-coloured centre. Render ALL feasible assignments and require exactly1 distinct output across their union. There is no ordered relaxation, hidden-cell cost, lexicographic output choice, first solution or arbitrary capped search. NumPy-free source uses ring-distance counts; independent gate constructs four explicit coordinate-set brackets, clips them and requires exact equality to visible colour cells.
draft_notes.domain_assumptions: Distinct frame colours; nonoverlapping visible frames; consecutive odd sizes; arm lengths1 for radius0,2 for radius1,2..radius thereafter; at least2 visible brackets for every noncentral frame. These are native random-constructor rules. We extend uniformly to arbitrary off-grid centres and an optional background-coloured centre to preserve every canonical fixture. The background must be the unique most frequent colour; the native13x13minimum grid and6-frame maximum imply background≥64cells while each frame≤36.
draft_notes.constructor_review: Native task_4290ef0e.py remains unchanged. All four canonical pairs satisfy the same broad class and each has exactly one answer across both size-start possibilities, including train3 with col=-1,row=height centres and the query with row=height and invisible background centre.
draft_notes.limitations: Arbitrary explicit parameters can violate the declared visibility/no-overlap/arm domain and can be unidentifiable. Saved identical-input witness differs by a single visible outer corner versus a central point; the outer-corner interpretation violates the two-visible-bracket requirement. We do not claim uniqueness among arbitrary renderings that bypass native sampling guards. Such limitations are explicit rather than resolved through centred-first heuristics.
